Core explanation · 00:00–04:59

I'm Dr.

Key details

  • Anand, Department of Electronics and Communication.
  • Today, we're going to see the logical operations.
  • A logical operation is an operation that acts on a binary number to produce the result according to the laws of Boolean logic.
  • A logic gate is a basic building block of digital circuits.
  • Logic gate is considered as a device that has the ability to produce one output level with a combination of input levels.
  • The function is represented f and Y is the result.
  • In continuation, logic gates are implemented by using diode transistors and by other several devices.
  • This logic gate can also be considered as electronic circuits.
  • The logic gate opened by diode is called diode resistive logic.
  • Inputs and outputs of logic gates are in two levels, which are termed as high and low, or true or false, or ON and OFF, simply one and zero.
  • Coming to the next step.
  • For all logic gates, a table with all the combination is listed below.
  • The combination of input variable and the corresponding output is termed as truth table, which is shown here.
  • It explains how the logic circuit output responds to various combination of logic level at the input.
  • AND operation is explained by the following truth table, where.
  • AND operation is A.B.
  • When inputs A and B are zero, zero, B results in zero.
  • Input zero and one multiplied to get zero.
  • One and zero, zero.
  • One and one is one.
  • This is also explained by a Venn diagram here.
  • The common is being highlighted here with the red color.
  • OR gate produces an output of logic one as shown in the diagram.
  • Even if one of the input is one state and produces an output of zero state if all the inputs are in the logic zero state.
  • OR operation is explained with the following table.
  • With zero, zero, we get zero.
  • With zero and one, and one and zero, and one and one, we get all one states.
  • The two diodes are connected in parallel here, and they're connected in series with a resistance with 1K.
  • With the input E is equal to 10, with input.
  • E1 and E2 here.
  • And that we can represent using a truth table with the input V1 in the one column,.
  • V2 second column, and V output in the third column.
  • The input V1 is also called as an input A, and similarly input two respectively with respect to V1 and V2.
  • When both the inputs are zero, zero, diodes are not forward biased and hence Vout is equal to zero.
  • If one of the input is 10 volts, so as shown in the diagram here, the first V input is 10 volts here, the second is zero, the diode one is forward biased hence we represent 0.7.
  • And what the difference between the applied voltage here and we calculate the Vout.
  • It's not 0.3, it's 0.7.
  • Here diodes are reverse connected compared to the previous one, and we connect a voltage E is equal to 10 volts here.
  • And applied voltage E1 and E2.
  • Because the difference between here is 0.7, so we get 0.7.

Example or application from the lecture

  • So we can build an example of AND, OR NOT functions.
  • Now consider the first condition here, zero, zero.
  • If one of the voltage we consider 10 volts here, so we consider this 10 volts and the second voltage is zero, diode is on.
